sources_considered.why: A research synthesis identifies shortcut learning across multiple settings. This version predates the post.
Controlled experiments compare successful inference models with tests designed to expose specific shortcuts.
Establishes the paper's authorship and version dates.
Material qualification: improvements on established image benchmarks transferred to newly collected tests.
Read to establish the intended distinction between benchmark scores and underlying capabilities; not used as outcome evidence.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; author manuscript of a Nature Machine Intelligence perspective
evidence_items.explanation: The perspective synthesizes a recurring mismatch between benchmark performance and performance under more demanding conditions. It supports the qualitative warning, but supplies no estimate of the fraction of all benchmark gains that are misleading.

Four models scored well on MNLI but generally performed poorly when the tested syntactic shortcuts gave incorrect answers. This establishes a concrete gap between benchmark success and reliable inference.

New CIFAR-10 and ImageNet tests produced lower absolute accuracy, but improvements between models still transferred. This limits any broader inference that benchmark progress generally disappears on independent testing; it does not refute the existence of recurring shortcut failures.

unresolved_gaps: The sources do not measure how frequently all AI benchmark gains are illusory.
